request.purpose: Quantify relative partition selectivity from observed endpoints and check whether the changing-selectivity hypothesis is distinguishable from alpha=1 or constant selectivity within supplied conservative error ranges.
request.model_spec: For each tie_line_id, use dilute and dense records in DATA['phase_measurements.json']; concentrations in ng/uL. Compute K_ref=Cr_dense/Cr_dilute and K_variant=Cv_dense/Cv_dilute when denominators are positive, then alpha=K_variant/K_ref. Propagate provided asymmetric errors as rectangular worst-case bounds: K_lo=(Cd-dense_lower)/(Cl+dilute_upper), K_hi=(Cd+dense_upper)/(Cl-dilute_lower), and alpha bounds as K_variant_lo/K_ref_hi and K_variant_hi/K_ref_lo when positive. Report exact status if any denominator is zero/nonpositive. Compare alpha point estimates and intervals across tie-line indices, explicitly stating that index is not established as composition. Null comparator: constant alpha=1 (nonselective relative partitioning); do not fit a composition response curve from three endpoints. Output the assay-matched conditional prediction and limitations separately from arithmetic results.

request.missing_relation: Whether composition-dependent partitioning or preferential enrichment in multicomponent RNA condensates can produce internal dilute domains/cavity morphology, and under what concentration, sequence, and phase conditions.
variables: dense and dilute phase concentrations (mass or molar concentration, if reported)
phase volumes or topology, if reported
request.conditions: Background first published on or before 2025-05-12; exclude target identity and later accounts. Prefer direct multicomponent RNA condensate evidence; distinguish full-text support from abstract-only support and flag non-RNA analogies.
request.query: (RNA condensate OR RNA phase separation) AND (multicomponent OR mixture OR compositional partitioning) AND (internal domains OR cavities OR vacuoles OR wetting OR morphology)
request.change_if_found: If a pre-cutoff source directly shows that composition-dependent preferential partitioning creates internal dilute domains in RNA-rich condensates, refine H1 to its reported species/concentration/phase conditions and derive a case-specific conditional prediction; if sources only show bulk coexistence or non-RNA analogies, keep the bridge speculative and use them only as alternatives or follow-up.

request.missing_relation: Whether RNA mixture composition controls internal multiphase domains or cavity morphology, beyond adsorption at external/coexisting-phase interfaces.
variables: solution conditions and concentrations if reported
request.conditions: Historical background first published on or before 2025-05-12; exclude target identity and later accounts. Distinguish direct RNA evidence from protein/RNA analogies; use abstract claims only within their stated support.
request.query: RNA mixture condensate internal domains morphology RNA composition wetting scaffold adsorbent multiphase cavities
request.change_if_found: If a pre-cutoff RNA mixture study directly reports composition-dependent internal domains or cavities, refine H1 to its observed species and conditions and state the transfer assumptions. If evidence remains limited to bulk coexistence or interface wetting, keep internal-cavity formation speculative and prioritize species-resolved imaging under fixed reaction chemistry.
